exported_nan_maxStride.note: NaN maxStride accepted by exported analyzeBlob

INVALID_NUMERIC_CONFIG.interpretation: Original R1 accepts NaN numeric options silently (scan runs with zero candidates = false success); no INVALID_CONFIGURATION, no SCAN_STARTED=NO marker.

EXCLUSION_CENSUS.interpretation: Original R1 records only INPUT_TOO_LARGE/ENTRY_TOO_LARGE/READER_FAILURE/SCAN_EXCEPTION/PER_SOURCE_CANDIDATE_CAP; FILTERED_EXTENSION/TOO_SMALL/FILTERED_REGEX are silent. DECLARED_ENTRIES != sum of recorded dispositions.

SAMPLE_VS_CENSUS.interpretation: Original R1 evaluates only the sampled rows; no FULL_CENSUS_* fields, no CENSUS_STATUS. In this fixture the evenly spread 1200-row sample sees a 100% valid ID column while the whole 4800-row table is 25% valid — the sample cannot and does not represent the full table.

SINGLE_DEFINITION_TABLE.interpretation: Original R1 exposes --min-distinct-id / minDistinctId (default 2). At minDistinctId=1 a single-definition table (all rows ID 4057) is detected; under the default it is silently excluded (explicit coverage restriction).

INTEGER_COUNTERS_AS_FLOATS.interpretation: Original R1 accepts subnormal f32 (u32 counters 1..5080 as bits) as in-range positions with rate 1.0 and reports no NAN/SUBNORMAL/INFINITY/u32-alternative diagnostics; subnormal candidates pass as ordinary position candidates.

NUMERIC_DAT_MODEL_NAME_PATTERN.interpretation: ids_from_export R1 accepts only .bnt/.ark model archives (a hypothetical .dat is rejected, NOT presented as a defect of the actual Models.bnt) and counts only <numeric>.nif names (non-numeric names silently excluded from S_model).

fixture.note: 10007 is prime: no stride in 12..512 divides it

LAYOUT_ATTEMPTS_VS_ADMITTED.interpretation: Original R1 increments layoutsTested only AFTER the divisibility and minRows filters, so a fully-visited-but-undividable buffer reports layoutsTested=0. Budget accounting on this quantity would charge 0 instead of 126.

XYZ_COLUMN_MEAN_VS_ROW_TRIPLE_RATE.interpretation: Original R1 xyzRate is the MEAN of the three per-axis column in-range rates (0.9 in this fixture). It is NOT the joint row-triple finite rate, which is 56/80=0.7 in this fixture (independently recomputed by the run countercheck).
